conclusion.reason: The research did not verify 100,000 active distinct employer sources with eligible remote software jobs. Provider totals, directory entries and job counts are different units.

method.employerNormalization: Lowercase employer name and remove all whitespace, matching the current company-comparison rule.
method.noveltyReference: Local stored Job Pool history; no private application or profile content was queried or sent to providers.
method.descriptionValidation: Full descriptions checked using the existing software occupation classifier and excluded-title rules; structured country/timezone metadata checked where available. Not manual verification of work authorization.
method.noDailyGuarantee: One snapshot cannot establish how many first-ever employers arrive each day. Himalayas pubDate means last updated, not original posting time.

localDatabase.limits: This is the database configured on this machine, not necessarily the Ubuntu production database. Companies use lowercase names with whitespace removed. A single snapshot measures recently posted employers, not first-ever employers or a guaranteed future daily supply.

historicalCatalogEvidence.remoteEligibilityInHistoricalExpansion: Not measured in the saved board-verification summaries.

headcountLabs.productionRecommendation: Promising breadth; requires a free account/key for REST. Trial daily freshness and employer novelty before integrating. Keep paid usage disabled and the spend cap at zero.
headcountLabs.freeAllowance: 100,000 delivered job/company/change-event records per organization per UTC month; re-fetches consume records again. This is not 100,000 employer sources.
headcountLabs.publicMcpUse: Small read-only research only. Public MCP terms prohibit automated bulk copying.

recommendations: Retain all current jobs and direct employer board imports; add Himalayas as a supplemental feed with visible attribution and its supplied applicationLink.
Default to one representative eligible job per company, with other roles expandable, while retaining all stored job records.
Exclude companies already applied to by the current user across that user's applications and profile-specific applied marks; retain an opt-in way to show them.

Track the first-ever encounter with a company separately from job publication, provider last-update and import times. Report newly encountered companies per rolling 24 hours and measure the arrival rate over multiple days.
Use stable company IDs/domains and curated aliases where possible, preserving the user's exact name-normalization matching as the baseline.
Do not generate placeholder boards, duplicate provider configurations or stale entries to reach a numerical source target.

providerTermsAndEvidence.finding: Free without a key, personal/commercial own-app display permitted; visible credit and supplied Himalayas applicationLink required. Keyed limits 60/min and 10,000/day. pubDate is last updated.
Official page lists REST API and MCP access as free.
Live keyless listing/detail API used in this research.
Free keyless public API; provider attribution and supplied application URL required.
Public free reads are personal/non-commercial; offering postings through a product to others requires an API plan.
100,000 records/month free; re-deliveries and changes count; quota and request caps must be enforced.
Own-app display permitted subject to terms and third-party rights; public MCP access is free but not for automated bulk copying.
Directory/snapshot can seed discovery, but the published dataset is frozen at October 5, 2026 and the live index shut down October 10.
Free public remote-job feed tested as a supplemental source.
Public API tested; no matching eligible US/UK/IE remote software employer in the first 300 records.

limitations: Name matches can miss spelling aliases; new means absent from this local pool snapshot, not never encountered by this user.
Provider samples have different sizes and completeness. Himalayas dates mean last update. Ocean listing-only candidates need description checks.
The local database last saw a job on October 21; gains versus a freshly importing Ubuntu deployment may be smaller.
Name-normalized companies are not verified legal entities, and aliases can inflate novelty.
Different provider sample sizes prevent treating the results as a complete market-share ranking.
The 165 combined company names are potential snapshot additions, not jobs imported, new sources created, or guaranteed new companies per day.

userTarget.definition: 1,000 distinct new employers per rolling 24 hours across the three countries combined, with previously applied-to employers excluded.
userTarget.measurementProxy: The current tests count distinct eligible companies and separately compare them to local Job Pool history. They do not measure the current user's unapplied companies.
userTarget.feasibility: Not demonstrated. The complete recent Freehire query yielded far fewer than 1,000 eligible company names; other provider samples do not establish a sustained 1,000-new-company daily rate. This is not proof of a market-wide impossibility.

dailySupplyMeasurement.scope: Current production Freehire role categories; remote; US/GB/IE or explicit worldwide; supported direct employer ATS sources only; existing excluded titles.
limitations: This is one rolling 24-hour snapshot from one provider, not a market-wide upper bound or a sustained daily rate.
Provider first-seen jobs can be old postings newly discovered by that provider. Source posting dates can be refreshed externally.
New company means a normalized name absent from local stored Job Pool history; user-specific application history was not queried.
Offset pagination is not a frozen snapshot; provider totals can change while paging.
dailySupplyMeasurement.important: The two windows overlap and must not be added. Provider first-seen and source posting dates describe different events. These are personal/non-commercial research calls, not a newly integrated feed.
